result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Section 337(a) sets a four-year period for an action upon a contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The stated scope is limited to unsecured written-contract claims.

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to the exception in Section 336a.
claims.note: The draft identifies the exception without claiming what Section 336a provides.

claims.claim: Section 337 does not state when the four-year period starts for an ordinary written-contract claim.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: This clause gives a duration but no starting event. The sale provision concerns secured obligations; the starting rules in (b) and (c) concern account stated and rescission, respectively.

claims.claim: The saved sources contain no other rule on when that period starts.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: CCP-337 is the only saved text. Its reference to Section 360 addresses extension, not the starting event.

result.summary: The sole saved text gives the period for the written-contract claim in scope but does not identify its starting event. The draft limits that conclusion to the saved sources.
